hypothesis: The simplest always-in currency trend: is any rule better than the council or FX-BT1?
rules: Every pair always held: LONG when the close is above its 100-day average, SHORT when below. Each pair sized 0.10 / its 63-day annualised volatility / 7; if the total is above 2x equity, all scaled down to 2x. Rebalanced at the first US session of each month and whenever any pair's direction flips.
rebalance_day: first US session of each month + direction flips
fills: decided after each US session close (17:15 New York) on OANDA daily mid candles; filled at the next forex day's open (17:00 New York, the instant after the close the rule read).
costs: same shared model as every league line: twins.config.SHARE_COSTS = 0 commission, 2 bps half spread, 3 bps slippage per trade (several times the real major-pair spread: conservative). Overnight financing (interest paid or earned on currency positions) is LEFT OUT, as in the registered FX-BT1 backtest: direction of the bias UNKNOWN.
data_needed: OANDA daily mid candles for the 7 pairs
window: forward only: version 1 from the first session after the lock to 31 Dec 2027 (roadmap Phase 2). No backtest stands behind this line in the league.
pass_bar: Roadmap Phase 4 (January 2028): passes if, after costs, it matched or beat the S&P 500 (Y-SPX), or came close with a clearly smaller worst fall, AND passes the luck check adjusted for 16 tries (deflated Sharpe: research_harness/harness/overfit.deflated_sharpe with n_trials = 16). The exact 'came close' and 'clearly smaller' numbers are UNKNOWN: Markus to fix them before version 1 starts.
